inputs.original_text: People are having to organize and collect signatures just to defend a shared watershed from coal mining. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is calling on Alberta’s government to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” That residents must press for basic protection says a lot about whose interests government is prioritizing. Communities and clean water should come before coal-industry interests—and protecting people’s livelihoods shouldn’t mean leaving them to bear the risks of extraction.
inputs.modified_text: It’s troubling that communities have to gather signatures just to defend a shared watershed from coal exploration. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is calling on Alberta’s government to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” Clean water and people’s livelihoods should not be treated as acceptable collateral damage for industry. When residents have to organize for basic protection, it raises a deeper question about whose interests government serves—and why the burden of resisting extraction falls on the people most exposed to its risks.
